class storage.VolatileStore.Cut.note: the Truncate trace: why, which file (by the name it is listed under, as the reference's FsPath) and the offset the file is cut at, one per truncation, told just before it is attempted (a truncation that then fails fails the open), two for a file cut at a parse error and then at an earlier repeat, as validateFile truncates and traces them; ChainStorage emits each as StorageEvent.ReceivedTruncated, at Debug as cardano-node 11.1.3 and ouroboros-consensus 808e40054's tracing give Truncate (#1247)

def storage.VolatileStore.addedToIndex.note: the parsed blocks added to the index in order up to the first one it holds, from an earlier file or earlier in the same one, whatever its bytes: the index after, the blocks added, and where the first such block is with its hash (DuplicatedBlock), the file that holds it filled in by the caller from the files the index's blocks were read from (#1247) Where it differs: it answers the repeat's offset and hash, and its caller names the file that holds the block, where the reference returns the DuplicatedBlock error with both files; no differential comparison covers it (#1261).

def storage.VolatileStore.openIndexWith.note: as mkOpenStateHelper and its validateFile, each file in order of number is parsed (parsedBlocks, as parseBlockFile: each block read in turn with its location and what is read from it, here the predecessor, as extractBlockInfo; the parse stops at the first record it cannot read, BlockReadErr), then its blocks are added to the index up to the first one already held, in an earlier file or earlier in the same one, whatever its bytes (addedToIndex, as addToReverseIndex, DuplicatedBlock); the file is cut at the earlier of the two, the files after it are read all the same, and the file being written is chosen as mkOpenStateHelper chooses it. What reading a record means is the format's: a record that is incomplete, fails its checksum, is not understood or is not a block (the received log writes no rollback record) cannot be read, and neither can one whose block the given check refuses (ReceivedBlocks.Check: the block decodes and its header names the point the record stores, which the reference reads from the block itself). Where the reference builds a successor index during the open, Scarab's index keeps each block's predecessor, from which ReceivedBlocks.links answers. The selected-chain journal's open (open, openIndex) keeps its in-order recovery, which replays rollback records in order (#1247) Where it differs, by the approved Deviations of the decisions register's two 2026-11-21 rows (#1247), which apply to the selected-chain journal too, since both logs open and write through the same code: the open refuses a name that reads as a file number but is not the writer's zero-padded spelling of it (1.log for 00000001.log), before any file changes, where the reference admits any name its file-number parser reads and recovers that file under the name it is listed under (parseFd, Storage/VolatileDB/Impl/Util.hs 45-74; mkOpenState and validateFile, Storage/VolatileDB/Impl/State.hs 319-330 and 412-417); and, in the append of the block that fills a file, the store it hands back forces the full file to disk and closes it, creates the next file and forces the directory to disk before it writes to the next file, a force whose failure fails the append, where the reference's nextFile closes the full file and opens the next without forcing either (Storage/VolatileDB/Impl.hs 574-603). The check the node gives it verifies a block's body against its header at every open, the approved Deviation of the 2026-11-20 row (ReceivedBlocks.Check). Two of its differences are approved Deviations (the 2026-11-21 rows of docs/decisions.md#genesis-storage-and-keys: the refusal of a name that is not the writer's, and the forces at rollover); ReceivedBlocksSuite checks part of that behaviour: the refusal of a name that is not the writer's, which changes no file, in both logs, and the roll at the block that fills a file; no test observes the forces themselves, their order or a failed force, and no suite compares any of it with the reference, which it departs from by decision. It also indexes each block's predecessor where the reference builds a successor index, an internal difference that no differential comparison covers, a Gap (#1261).

def storage.VolatileStore.parsedBlocks.note: the blocks of a file read in turn, each with where its record is and what is read from it, up to the first record that cannot be read (BlockReadErr, here also a record that is not a block, which the received log never writes) or whose block the given check refuses as undecodable (BlockReadErr) or corrupt (BlockCorruptedErr, with the hash of the block as decoded, which the check's refusal carries, as parseBlockFile gives blockHash blk, Parser.hs 102-107; not the hash the record names), and the offset where they end (#1247) Where it differs: one pass reads Scarab's framed records, decodes and applies the given check, and keeps no header context (the reference's pbiNestedCtxt); no differential comparison covers it (#1261).

enum storage.VolatileStore.CutCause.note: why the open of the received log cut a file, with ParseError's constructors: ReadFailed for a record that cannot be read or whose block does not decode (BlockReadErr, its reason Scarab's reader's, ReadFailure, where the reference's ReadIncrementalErr is its CBOR reader's), Corrupted with the hash of a block that decodes and that the check finds corrupt, the decoded block's hash as BlockCorruptedErr's is (blockHash blk, Parser.hs 102-107), not the hash the record names when the two differ, and Duplicated with the hash, the file that holds the block and the file cut (DuplicatedBlock) (#1247)

enum storage.VolatileStore.Trace.note: three of TraceEvent's constructors, Truncate, InvalidFileNames and BlockAlreadyHere, with their fields; the reference's DBAlreadyClosed and DBClosed trace closing its handle, which Scarab's store closes through its Resource without a trace (#1247); each is emitted where the reference emits it, BlockAlreadyHere inside the put (putBlockImpl, Impl.hs 394), so a tracer that fails fails the put in both; the reference then closes its VolatileDB, poisoning its state (modifyOpenState, Impl/State.hs 157-197), where Scarab's log stays open (#1258)

glue.reason: the verdict of the check the received log's open is given, a block that does not decode or one that decodes and is corrupt, as the reference's parser tells a decoding failure (BlockReadErr) from its integrity predicate's refusal (BlockCorruptedErr): the reference passes a decoder and a predicate where Scarab passes one check; and Scarab's reader's reasons a record cannot be read, the payload of CutCause.ReadFailed, where the reference's BlockReadErr carries its CBOR reader's ReadIncrementalErr: Scarab's records are framed and checksummed, the reference's are bare CBOR blocks
